subject: Mathematics
title: Priya's Toy Giveaway
hook: How do you give away toys when you don't have enough ones?

slides.title: The Toy Problem
slides.storyContext: Priya has 32 toys and wants to give away 15 toys to her cousin. But there's a catch: She has only 2 ones and needs to give away 5!
slides.inSimpleWords: Sometimes we need to borrow from tens!

image.alt: The Toy Problem — Subtraction with Borrowing

slides.title: Set Up the Problem
slides.storyContext: Ravi writes it down: 32 on top, 15 below it. 'Ones under ones, tens under tens!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Ones line up with ones, tens with tens.

image.alt: Set Up the Problem — Subtraction with Borrowing

slides.title: The Problem in Ones
slides.storyContext: Priya tries: 2 - 5 = ? 'Wait! I can't take 5 from 2. I need more ones!'

example.solution: We can't! So we need to borrow from the tens.

slides.inSimpleWords: 2 is too small to subtract 5 from.

image.alt: The Problem in Ones — Subtraction with Borrowing

slides.title: Borrow a Ten
slides.storyContext: Ravi says, 'One of your 3 tens can become 10 ones! Take 1 ten from the tens.' Priya has 2 tens left and 12 ones now!

points.label: Borrowing
points.text: Break 1 ten into 10 ones. So 3 tens become 2 tens, and 2 ones become 12 ones.

image.alt: Borrow a Ten — Subtraction with Borrowing

slides.title: Subtract the Ones
slides.storyContext: Now Priya has 12 ones. 'Twelve minus five is... 7!' She writes 7 in the ones place.

image.alt: Subtract the Ones — Subtraction with Borrowing

slides.title: Subtract the Tens
slides.storyContext: After borrowing, Priya has 2 tens left. 'Two tens minus 1 ten equals 1 ten.' She writes 1 in the tens place.

image.alt: Subtract the Tens — Subtraction with Borrowing

slides.title: The Answer
slides.storyContext: Ravi checks: 1 ten and 7 ones = 17. 'So 32 - 15 = 17 toys left!'

slides.title: Another Example: 41 - 26
slides.storyContext: Ravi tries a new one. 1 - 6 won't work, so borrow 1 ten. Now 11 - 6 = 5. Then 3 - 2 = 1. Answer: 15!

slides.title: Why Borrow?
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'When ones are too small, we break a ten into 10 ones. It's like exchanging a big coin for 10 small ones!'

slides.title: Try: 53 - 28
slides.storyContext: Ravi writes: 3 - 8 won't work. Borrow 1 ten! 13 - 8 = 5. Then 4 - 2 = 2. Answer: 25!

points.label: Practice
points.text: 53 - 28 = 25. Borrow from tens, subtract ones, subtract tens.

slides.title: Priya's Gift Complete
slides.storyContext: Priya counts 17 toys remaining. 'Borrowing helped me solve the problem. When ones aren't enough, we borrow from tens!'

points.label: Summary
points.text: 1. Check if ones can be subtracted. 2. If not, borrow 1 ten (becomes 10 ones). 3. Subtract ones. 4. Subtract tens (remember you borrowed!). 5. Write the answer.

slides.inSimpleWords: Borrowing is trading 1 ten for 10 ones!

image.alt: Priya's Gift Complete — Subtraction with Borrowing

subject: Mathematics
title: Ravi's Bakery Helper Adventure
hook: Can Ravi arrange cookies in perfect groups for the bakery?

slides.title: Cookies by the Box
slides.storyContext: Priya is packing cookies. 'Ravi, put 2 cookies in each box. If I have 5 boxes, how many cookies do we need?'

image.alt: Cookies by the Box — Multiplication Tables 2-5

slides.title: Table of 2
slides.storyContext: Ravi lines up cookies: 2, then 4, then 6, then 8, then 10! 'I see a pattern, Priya! It goes up by 2 each time!'

slides.title: 2 Times Tables (Repetition)
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches: 1×2=2, 2×2=4, 3×2=6, 4×2=8, 5×2=10. 'See? Ravi, each number gets the pattern!'

slides.title: Table of 5
slides.storyContext: Now Priya uses fingers to count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50! 'Look at your hands, Ravi! Each hand has 5 fingers!'

slides.title: 5 Times Tables
slides.storyContext: Ravi uses fingers: 1×5=5 (one hand), 2×5=10 (two hands), 3×5=15, and so on!

slides.title: Table of 3 and 4
slides.inSimpleWords: Tables of 3 and 4 have their own patterns!

slides.title: Multiplication Story
slides.storyContext: Priya asks, 'Ravi, if I have 4 cookie boxes with 5 cookies in each, how many cookies total?'

slides.title: Comparing Tables
slides.storyContext: Ravi notices: '2×5=10, but 5×2 also=10!' Priya smiles. 'The order doesn't matter in multiplication, Ravi!'

example.solution: Yes! Both equal 10. Multiplication works both ways.

slides.title: Quick Recall
slides.storyContext: Priya writes all tables on the wall. 'Ravi, let's practice saying them fast: 2×3=6, 3×4=12, 5×5=25! Soon you'll know them by heart!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Practice tables until they become automatic!

slides.title: The Market
slides.storyContext: At the market, Ravi sees: 'Apples are ₹3 each. If I buy 5 apples, how much is it?' 5×3=15, so ₹15!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Multiplication helps with money and shopping!

slides.title: Tables Learned!
slides.storyContext: Priya and Ravi sit tired but happy. 'We learned that multiplication is groups and repeated adding. Tables 2, 3, 4, 5 are our new friends!'

points.label: Final
points.text: 1. Multiplication = groups. 2. Table of 2: 2,4,6,8,10... 3. Table of 5: 5,10,15,20,25... 4. Table of 3 and 4 have patterns too. 5. Use for shopping and real problems!

slides.inSimpleWords: Multiplication tables help us count groups fast!

subject: Mathematics
title: Priya's Festival Market
hook: Can Ravi count enough rupees to buy all the festival treats?

slides.title: Festival Day Shopping
slides.storyContext: It's festival day! Ravi has coins and notes in his pocket. 'Priya, help me count my money! I want to buy sweets!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Indian money has coins and colorful notes!

slides.title: Indian Coins
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi: 'Look! Small ₹1 coin, then ₹2, then ₹5, then big ₹10 coin. Each is worth different amounts!'

slides.title: Indian Notes
slides.storyContext: Priya pulls out paper money: 'Here's a red ₹10 note, then a blue-green ₹20 note, then a pink ₹50 note! Each worth more!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Notes are colorful and worth more money!

slides.title: Counting Coins
slides.storyContext: Ravi counts: 'I have 3 rupees in ₹1 coins, plus 1 rupee in a ₹5 coin... wait! That's just 1 rupee, not 5 rupees!'

slides.title: Counting Notes
slides.storyContext: Priya counts: 'One ₹50 note, one ₹20 note, one ₹10 note. That's 50 + 20 + 10 = 80 rupees!'

example.problem: Count: one ₹50 note + one ₹20 note + one ₹10 note.

slides.title: Mixed Money
slides.storyContext: Ravi now counts everything: '2 rupees in coins plus 80 rupees in notes. That's ₹82 total! Will it buy my sweets?'

slides.title: Shopping at the Stall
slides.storyContext: The sweet seller says, 'Laddu is ₹10 each. Jalebi is ₹15 a plate. Kheer costs ₹20.' Ravi thinks hard!

example.problem: Ravi has ₹30. Can he buy 1 Jalebi (₹15) and 1 Kheer (₹20)?
example.solution: ₹15 + ₹20 = ₹35. No, he needs ₹5 more. He has only ₹30.

image.alt: Shopping at the Stall — Money Counting

slides.title: Making Change
slides.storyContext: Priya says, 'If your ₹50 note pays for ₹30 worth of sweets, the seller gives you ₹20 change. 50 - 30 = 20!'

points.label: Change
points.text: Money given - Money spent = Change left

slides.inSimpleWords: Change is money you get back!

slides.title: Real Purchase
slides.storyContext: Ravi buys 2 laddus (₹10 each) and 1 jalebi (₹15). He pays with ₹50. How much change?

slides.title: Different Coins Make Same Value
slides.storyContext: Priya shows: 'Five ₹2 coins = 1 ₹10 coin. Same value, different coins!' Ravi's eyes light up.

example.problem: Are five ₹2 coins worth the same as one ₹10 coin?

slides.inSimpleWords: Different coins can make the same amount!

image.alt: Different Coins Make Same Value — Money Counting

slides.title: Money Mastered!
slides.storyContext: Ravi eats his sweets happily. 'Priya, I know coins and notes now! Counting money is like counting numbers!'

points.label: Learning
points.text: 1. Indian coins: ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10. 2. Indian notes: ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100. 3. Add coins and notes together. 4. Check prices. 5. Calculate change. 6. Money math is number math!
